[INVENTED TEST TEXT written for the WhatIf ATL test suite. This is not real reporting; the names, numbers and quotes are made up.]

Study: Clifton Corridor rail would pull 4,000 new riders

A consultant's study of a light rail line from Lindbergh Center to Emory says the line would add 4,000 new daily riders and lift transit's share of commutes in the corridor from 30% to 35%. The average commute for residents along the route would fall to 24 minutes.

The price is steep: $2.1 billion before financing. The study also warns that 1,100 renter households near the stations could be priced out within a decade, and that only 18% of the travel-time benefit would reach formerly redlined neighborhoods.

Emory officials declined to comment.
